ai.description: *Raorchestes chotta* is a tiny bushfrog (15–17 mm) with a brown dorsum and distinct dark brown lateral bands. It features a pointed snout and lacks webbing on the fingers and toes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes chotta* is best distinguished by its tiny size (<18 mm) and the presence of a distinct, dark, inverted V-shaped marking on its back between the shoulders.
ai.habitat: The Small Bushfrog inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests and shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Raorchestes chotta is primarily nocturnal, spending its nights actively foraging for small insects among the foliage of low-lying shrubs and bushes.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes chotta* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. It breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in leaf axils or hollows.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes chotta* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically found in the high-elevation shola forests of Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
ai.callDescription: The Small Bushfrog emits a high-pitched, insect-like "tseep-tseep" call, typically heard from vegetation in high-altitude shola forests and grasslands.
